flags.message: The self-represented applicant’s signature block in application.txt retains part of a mailing address, although documents.json reports zero contact residuals. Please review the scrub around signature blocks followed by an appendix. The residual is omitted from the forecast and had no bearing on it.

Snapshot 2026-11-26.json carries an inherited pre-docketing conference distribution ('Sep 16 2026: DISTRIBUTED for Conference of 10/9/2026' -> 'Oct 13 2026: Motion Granted') from linked miscellaneous sealing motion 26M23 before No. 26-502 was docketed on October 15, 2026. As a result, context.json freezes distribution_count=2 and band='elevated' even though the November 24, 2026 distribution (for the December 11, 2026 Conference) is the cert petition's first distribution and arrives on waivers from both respondents.

The frozen count of two distributions and elevated band include the October 9 conference, which preceded the October 13 sealing-motion grant and October 15 petition docketing. December 11 appears to be the first conference on certiorari. Treating this as a substantive relist could materially inflate the scoring baseline.

The frozen distribution_count of 2 (band `elevated`, cert_anchor 0.248) appears to count a motion-only conference as a distribution of the petition. The Sep 16 entry 'DISTRIBUTED for Conference of 10/9/2026' precedes docketing (Oct 15) and the response deadline and is followed by 'Motion Granted' (Oct 13) on the motion for leave to file under seal (linked 26M23). The Nov 24 distribution for the 12/11/2026 conference looks like the petition's first, after both respondents waived. The petition was likely never relisted, so the band and anchor probably overstate its grant likelihood; I forecast well below the anchor on that reading.

lower-court-docket.txt reports the Supreme Court judgment date as unavailable and says this prevented a bounded rehearing lookup. The snapshot's LowerCourtDecision field contains 'April 21, 2026
Rule 12.4'. The joint petition confirms that date for Nathan and separately dates the Cribbs Ringer judgment, so the forecast could use both.

The November 24 entry labeled “Reply of Christopher Dier submitted” links a readable reply PDF. The staged documents manifest omitted it. The reply was retrieved from the snapshot link and considered, including its discussion of Stone and the competing petitions.

The rendered statpack band table is labeled sal-v8 while context.json freezes sal-v9. The JSON includes sal-v9 among the alternative segments. For this private baseline petition both versions yield 656 grants in 12,668 prior-Term cases, matching the frozen anchor. The version difference had no numerical effect.

metrics/statpack.md's 'Segment base rate by salience band' table is headed sal-v8 while record/context.json froze band 'baseline' under sal-v9. I anchored on the frozen cert_anchor.rate (0.052); the class-floor fallback for a private petitioner (baseline reached rate) gives about the same figure, so the forecast is unaffected.

The Markdown salience table is labeled sal-v8, while context.json freezes sal-v9. The JSON statpack includes sal-v9 as an alternate series and reproduces the frozen rate (656/12,668). The private-petitioner floor in the displayed series gives the same rate.

metrics/statpack.md heads its band table 'Segment base rate by salience band (sal-v8)' while record/context.json carries salience_version sal-v9. Band is baseline, which is also the private caption-class floor, and I anchored on the frozen cert_anchor.rate (0.0518) and cert_amicus_line, so the forecast is unaffected.

Salience-version heading mismatch between record/context.json (salience_version='sal-v9', which carries a valid non-null cert_anchor.rate=0.051784 pooled from statpack.json's sal-v9 series) and metrics/statpack.md's rendered table heading ('Segment base rate by salience band (sal-v8)', where the private-petitioner baseline reached floor across OT2017-OT2025 is 5.20%, 659/12668). Both figures agree at ~5.2%.

The rendered statpack labels the salience table sal-v8 while context.json freezes sal-v9. The JSON pack's sal-v9 rows reproduce the frozen baseline of 656/12,668, so the forecast used the matching rate.

metrics/statpack.md heads its per-Term salience band table sal-v8 while record/context.json carries salience_version sal-v9. I anchored on the frozen cert_anchor.rate (0.0518), which matches the private-caption baseline floor either way.

record/context.json assigns salience_version 'sal-v9' (with frozen cert_anchor.rate = 0.05178402273444901 under statpack_digest sha256:43224abac2bb0f0345ecf1f208a4c5c1229f4514030d2604ba6ab51a139bed19), whereas the checked-out metrics/statpack.md renders 'Segment base rate by salience band (sal-v8)' (sha256:14812795... on metrics/statpack.json, which holds sal-v9 in alt_segments). Per the prompt's salience-version rule, I anchored on cert_anchor.rate and cross-checked the private caption-class floor ('baseline' reached over OT2017-OT2025), both of which equal 656 / 12,668 = 0.05178402273444901.

The salience table in metrics/statpack.md displays sal-v8. The cell uses sal-v9. The prior-Term private-petitioner floor and the sal-v9 alternate rows in metrics/statpack.json both reproduce the frozen 5.1784% grant rate (656 of 12,668).

metrics/statpack.md's 'Segment base rate by salience band' table is headed sal-v8 while record/context.json froze this cell's band under sal-v9. Anchored on the frozen cert_anchor.rate (0.0518) and the baseline (private caption class) floor rather than reading the band off the table.

The salience table in metrics/statpack.md is labeled sal-v8, while the cell uses sal-v9. The private-petitioner reached rate pooled over OT2017–25 is identical under both versions in metrics/statpack.json and reproduces the frozen 5.1784% anchor. The version difference had no numerical effect.
context.json carries salience_version sal-v9 but the committed metrics/statpack.md band table is headed sal-v8. I anchored on the frozen cert_anchor.rate (0.052) and did not pool the table.

metrics/statpack.md renders 'Segment base rate by salience band (sal-v8)', whereas record/context.json assigns band 'federal' under salience_version 'sal-v9'. Both context.json's pre-pooled cert_anchor.rate (from statpack.json's sal-v9 alt_segments) and the federal caption-class reached floor over OT2017-OT2025 equal 155/212 (0.7311), so the rendered markdown heading lag does not change the anchor.
The Markdown statpack labels the band table sal-v8, while the cell froze sal-v9. The JSON statpack includes both versions and their prior-Term federal rates agree with the frozen anchor.
